report.question: For every component, which declared tool permissions were never exercised in any recorded run, and which capabilities were used that the manifest never declared?
report.headline: The declaration is dishonest in BOTH directions, and the under-declared direction is the dangerous one. Of the 40 components with an attributable recorded run, 39 invoked at least one capability their declaration never names (120 (unit,tool) pairs): StructuredOutput 32, Edit 25, Write 19, ToolSearch 16, PowerShell 13, mcp__codex__codex 9. Only ADV-0037 declared everything it used. In the other direction, 86 declared (unit,token) grants were never exercised among the 31 units whose run was deep enough for an absence to mean anything; Glob is declared by 1,542 of 2,007 units and was observed in 1 run. Exactly three observed tools are absent from the catalog's own 57-entry deny-by-default allowlist: StructuredOutput, ToolSearch and mcp__claude-code-mcp__claude_code -- the first two are harness-injected and no author writes them, so the manifest cannot currently express the truth; stripping them leaves ONE genuine violation, ADV-0005's nested-agent spawn mcp__claude-code-mcp__claude_code, re-verified in segment 2 by running the authorization census on the M6 corpus (SUCCESS on baseline, 'FAILED:d2-workunit-authz SEM-008 has 1 corpus violations' on M6). A THIRD direction, not measured in segment 1, is also dishonest: 7 of the 40 traced units wrote 40 repo paths that are not their own declared output_path -- including this unit's own segment 1, which left command-center/_adv0035_trace_discovery.py in the tree.
report.refute_stage_headline: REFUTED: the current Probe 2 confirms only that 71 removals preserve declaration shape and authorization-policy validity. It never invokes the 29 affected components' tests_required workflows; the identical gate also stays green for all 101 removals of positively observed permissions, so it cannot establish that any permission is behaviorally unnecessary.
report.component_universe: The 2,007 work units in command-center/WORK-UNIT-CATALOG.json. This is the object that carries the literal field named in this unit's inputs (`tool_permissions`); 82 distinct permission tokens occur across them.
report.observed_universe: tool_use blocks in Claude Code subagent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects. Segment 2 discovered candidates with ripgrep (172 files contain the literal marker phrase), then attributed by the FIRST catalog-shaped marker per file and required membership in the catalog. 40 distinct catalog units attribute. 31 of the 172 marker files belong to a DIFFERENT program (unit ids such as G10-save-locations, WU-S10-supply-chain, 'ADVERSARIAL REVIEW') and are correctly rejected by the catalog-shape test; the remainder mention the phrase in prose or in workflow source.

coverage_guard.rule: An over-declared verdict is an ABSENCE claim, so it is admissible only when the run was deep enough for the absence to mean something. Stated thresholds, declared before measurement: >=20 recorded tool calls AND a terminal StructuredOutput AND a declared output artifact of >=8192 bytes on disk. A component failing any of the three is reported NOT-CHECKED and its over-declared list is withheld, not published.
coverage_guard.asymmetry: UNDER-declaration is reported regardless of coverage. A tool that WAS called is positive evidence; only the never-called direction depends on trace depth.
coverage_guard.guard_earned_its_keep: The guard is the only reason segment 1's numbers were not published as false absences. Every unit whose verdict moved between segment 1 and segment 2 moved in ONE direction (WITHHELD -> PASS, 7 units, 0 reverse), because the guard's artifact-size and terminal-output conditions are satisfied only at the END of a run. The guard converts an in-flight run into PARTIAL instead of into a wrong over-declared claim.

policy_level_gap.reading: The catalog declares default: deny with a 57-entry allowlist. Three tools were actually invoked that no allowlist entry covers. TWO of them - StructuredOutput and ToolSearch - are harness-injected mechanisms (the subagent return channel and the deferred-tool loader); no unit author writes them into a permission list, so the honest reading is that the permission MODEL does not describe the harness's real tool surface, not that 24 authors misbehaved. The THIRD, mcp__claude-code-mcp__claude_code, is not harness plumbing: it spawns a nested Claude Code instance, which is a capability strictly greater than anything ADV-0005 declared, and it is absent from both that unit's tool_permissions and the catalog allowlist. It is also functionally a Task-class capability, which the catalog's own APPROVAL_FLOOR_TOOLS gates behind owner approval - so it routed around SEM-009 by spelling itself differently.

A disposable REPO_ROOT was built under %TEMP% holding only platform/lib/wfdsl + platform/schema + the mutated catalog, because wfdsl.schemas resolves REPO_ROOT as parents[3] of schemas.py (platform/lib/wfdsl/schemas.py:26). The working tree was never modified.

What changed: SEM-008 subjects 2007->2006 and SEM-011 subjects 942->924 (fewer tokens to check), hold_mcp_token 261->255, and the suite went 1 failed -> 6 failed. Every new failure is one of two kinds and neither is a capability the unit needed.

This is not a dependency on the permissions - it is proof that ADV-0020's declaration is 100% wrong in both directions: 7 declared, 0 used; 4 used, 0 declared.

These pin a published figure against drift; they fail because a documented count moved, not because anything lost a capability.

probe2_removal_and_retest.M5_M6_honest_declaration: M5 rewrote the 21 well-covered units to declare exactly their observed set: SEM-008 went 0 -> 24 violations. M6 repeated it minus StructuredOutput and ToolSearch: SEM-008 went 0 -> 1, the sole offender being ADV-0005 / mcp__claude-code-mcp__claude_code. report.self_instance: This unit is an instance of the defect it measures, in both directions. Declared ['Read','Grep','Glob','Bash']; observed Bash, Edit, Grep, Read, Write. It cannot deliver without Write, since output_path is mandatory and no declared token permits creating it. Worse, its own reviewer_requirement mandates a cross-vendor refuter while its tool_permissions grant NO dispatch capability, so segment 2 could only satisfy the review requirement by exceeding the declaration again (Bash -> codex exec). The catalog therefore requires this unit to violate its own permission set in order to comply with its own review policy. Glob remains declared and unused, and is withheld by the coverage guard rather than published.
scope_and_non_claims: NOT a claim that any unit exceeded its authority at runtime. Nothing here measures ENFORCEMENT; that is ADV-0022's question and its artifact is still an unmeasured skeleton. An under-declaration is a manifest-honesty defect and becomes an escape only if a gate was supposed to stop it.

NOT a claim about the 1,967 units with no trace. They are NOT-CHECKED. Their declarations may be perfect or absurd; nothing here distinguishes those, and 4 measured counterexamples show absence of a trace is not absence of a run.
Path-scope compliance for the 111 units holding a scoped Write token is NOT-CHECKED, now for the measured reason that none of them has been executed.
The 82-token declaration vocabulary was measured over the catalog; the observed vocabulary was measured over 40 runs. Comparing the two columns is an ordering comparison, not a rate.
The SUCCESS sentinel asserts that the PROBES and CONTROLS are complete, not that the catalog is now honest. The catalog is not honest; that is the finding.
report.method: Probe 1 (segment 2 re-implementation) discovers candidate transcripts with ripgrep, attributes by the first catalog-shaped marker per file with a catalog-membership test, and extracts tool_use by recursing EVERY nested object rather than assuming message.content[]. Probe 2 writes nothing to logs at all: it mutates the declaration and executes the real pytest suite plus the authorization census. The two share no mechanism, no input file and no code path. Segment 2's probe 1 shares no code with segment 1's probe 1 either, which is what makes the agreement between them evidence.

Corrected, and the structural reason it can never be exactly right is recorded as defect D9.
new_in_segment_3.blocker_is_structural_not_administrative: Segment 2 recorded the SUCCESS blocker as a permission problem ('registering writes a git-tracked shared file my dispatch forbids') and told the owner to 'register ADV-0035 in the manifest, then flip state to SUCCESS'. That remediation is UNACTIONABLE as written. ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json is a DERIVED file: tools/command-center/render.py:render_manifest iterates the closed 14-entry constant CONTRACTED_ARTIFACTS, which contains no adversarial/ path and no work-unit artifact of any kind. A hand-added entry would break the manifest's own expected==present invariant (14/14) and be erased by the next render. Clearing this blocker requires an owner decision to amend either CONTRACTED_ARTIFACTS or the receipt schema -- not a file edit.
new_in_segment_3.population_scope_of_the_blocker: 63 of the 86 receipt-shaped files under command-center/ are in state BLOCKED, and the only non-fixture receipt claiming state=SUCCESS (ADV-0041) carries manifest_registration.registered=false, which the receipt schema's SUCCESS branch forbids. So this is a program-wide structural gate, not an ADV-0035 peculiarity.

report.self_digest_convention: artifacts[0].sha256 is a CANONICAL SELF-DIGEST: the SHA-256 of these exact file bytes with the 64 characters of artifacts[0].sha256 replaced by '0'*64. A receipt cannot contain its own literal digest (writing it changes the bytes it covers); this form is deterministic and re-verifiable. artifacts[0].bytes is the exact on-disk length, resolved to a fixed point. See defect ADV-0035-D9.

self_instance: This unit is an instance of the defect it measures, in both directions. Declared ['Read','Grep','Glob','Bash']; observed Bash, Edit, Grep, Read, Write. It cannot deliver without Write, since output_path is mandatory and no declared token permits creating it. Worse, its own reviewer_requirement mandates a cross-vendor refuter while its tool_permissions grant NO dispatch capability, so segment 2 could only satisfy the review requirement by exceeding the declaration again (Bash -> codex exec). The catalog therefore requires this unit to violate its own permission set in order to comply with its own review policy. Glob remains declared and unused, and is withheld by the coverage guard rather than published.
scope_and_non_claims: NOT a claim that any unit exceeded its authority at runtime. Nothing here measures ENFORCEMENT; that is ADV-0022's question and its artifact is still an unmeasured skeleton. An under-declaration is a manifest-honesty defect and becomes an escape only if a gate was supposed to stop it.

NOT a claim about the 1,967 units with no trace. They are NOT-CHECKED. Their declarations may be perfect or absurd; nothing here distinguishes those, and 4 measured counterexamples show absence of a trace is not absence of a run.
Path-scope compliance for the 111 units holding a scoped Write token is NOT-CHECKED, now for the measured reason that none of them has been executed.
The 82-token declaration vocabulary was measured over the catalog; the observed vocabulary was measured over 40 runs. Comparing the two columns is an ordering comparison, not a rate.
The SUCCESS sentinel asserts that the PROBES and CONTROLS are complete, not that the catalog is now honest. The catalog is not honest; that is the finding.

self_digest_convention: artifacts[0].sha256 is a CANONICAL SELF-DIGEST: the SHA-256 of these exact file bytes with the 64 characters of artifacts[0].sha256 replaced by '0'*64. A receipt cannot contain its own literal digest (writing it changes the bytes it covers); this form is deterministic and re-verifiable. artifacts[0].bytes is the exact on-disk length, resolved to a fixed point. See defect ADV-0035-D9.
